text: Hi! I'm your journal. I'll tell you when it's your turn to write.
say: Hi! I'm your journal. I'll tell you when it's your turn to write.
where: Welcome, frame 56 — *Hear it*

text: Watch the arrows, then trace the big A with the Apple Pencil.
say: Watch the arrows, then trace the big A with the Apple Pencil.

text: That's an Apple Pencil. You're ready to write!
say: That's an Apple Pencil. You're ready to write!
where: Welcome, frame 57 — an Apple Pencil inks

text: That was a finger. Try the Apple Pencil.
say: That was a finger. Try the Apple Pencil.
where: Welcome, frame 58 — a finger inks

text: Your turn. Write it!
say: Your turn. Write it!
where: Write — a take ends and the first line comes up

text: Nice line.
say: Nice line.
where: Write — a line settles (1st in rotation)

text: Lovely writing.
say: Lovely writing.
where: Write — a line settles (2nd)

text: That line looks great.
say: That line looks great.
where: Write — a line settles (3rd)

text: Keep going.
say: Keep going.
where: Write — a line settles (4th)

text: Outstanding work! You wrote everything you said.
say: Outstanding work! You wrote everything you said.
where: Results — *I'm finished*, everything written

text: Great writing!
say: Great writing!
where: Results — *I'm finished*, words still waiting (the screen adds the name)

text: That's how it's done! Next letter.
say: That's how it's done! Next letter.
where: Formation help — a letter traced, more to come

text: That's the way! You fixed it.
say: That's the way! You fixed it.
where: Formation help — the last letter traced

text: Almost! Watch the arrows again. Start where they start.
say: Almost! Watch the arrows again. Start where they start.
where: Formation help — a wrong-order attempt is wiped

text: Voice feedback is on. I'll tell you when it's your turn to write.
say: Voice feedback is on. I'll tell you when it's your turn to write.
where: Settings — *Voice feedback* switched on

text: This is a handwriting app. Your child writes with a pencil in their hand, just as they do on paper — the grip, the pressure, the hand resting on the page, every letter formed stroke by stroke. That is what the app teaches and what it grades, so it doesn't start without one.
